title: How keratin cortex thickness affects iridescent feather colours
why_selected: TEM/electron micrographs (Figs 2-3) of the keratin-cortex + melanosome multilayer in iridescent blue (480 nm) and green (520 nm) common-pheasant barbules; quantitative cortex/melanosome nm data and etch-induced peak shifts. Directly on-topic, CC BY.

title: Prediction of individual differences in non-iridescent structural plumage colour from nanostructural periodicity and regularity
why_selected: Fig 1b TEM of spongy keratin nanostructure of the blue-tit blue crown; non-iridescent UV-blue; SAXS periodicity (q~0.045 & 0.075 nm^-1). Core spongy-keratin structural-colour paper, CC BY.

title: Sexual dichromatism, size dimorphism, and microscale anatomy of white wing stripe in blue tits
why_selected: Fig 1C/1D SEM cross-sections of blue-tit greater-covert barbs from the blue vane and the white wing-stripe dot, labelling cortex/spongy/air-vacuoles/melanosomes. Two structural colours (blue + white) in one SEM figure.

title: Effect of nanostructural irregularities on structural color in the tail feathers of the Oriental magpie Pica serica
why_selected: Fig 2B SEM + Fig 2C TEM of the hexagonal melanin-rod stack (Durrell type 5) producing iridescent green/blue/violet domains; reflectance peak ~520 nm (Fig 3). Melanosome-array structural colour, CC BY.

title: Melanin-based structural coloration of birds and its biomimetic applications
why_selected: Review (Appl. Microscopy, CC BY) with electron-micrograph figures naming many species+colour pairs: Steller's jay blue barb, Lawes's parotia, green-winged teal, violet-backed starling, racket-tail hummingbird, rock dove; plus coherent-scattering / amorphous-nanostructure mechanism used to justify spongy-blue species. Article licence does not cover all reproduced third-party images; consult image-level Supplementary S1 and docs/RIGHTS_CORRECTION_20261018.md.

title: Genetic Basis and Evolution of Structural Color Polymorphism in an Australian Songbird
why_selected: White-winged fairywren (Malurus leucopterus): text establishes that the spongy medullary keratin layer produces structural blue (blue males), with melanin/cortex changes making other morphs black. Figures are schematic (no EM), so used for mechanism/colour provenance only.

title: Alcedo atthis (common kingfisher) reference; non-iridescent cyan-blue from spongy medullary keratin
why_selected: Project namesake. No open-access SEM figure of Alcedo atthis was fetchable; the kingfisher record uses the species' well-documented cyan-blue plumage colour with the spongy-keratin mechanism cross-cited to PMC10962638/PMC8505553. Panel is a synthetic proxy, clearly flagged.
